what: The speedup ladder, first pass (2026-09-03): three bank scenes chosen for their failure surfaces, each rendered from the TRUE baseline (stock attention, no LoRA) up through sage alone, sage+Sol as shipped, sage fp16+Sol, and shipped PDD8 (sage+Sol on the PDD sidecar). Matched seed, 1344x768, 345 frames. Judged blind by the owner with free-text notes; timing rows are a by-product on an unarmed server. Base and PDD rungs are separate ladders that share a scene, never pooled.

scenes.standoff: t2va_frontier_standoff -- two speakers, a figure at distance, a painted sign, a silent bystander
scenes.diner: t2va_diner_breakup -- close-up two-person dialogue over scored music: the audio-judgeable one
scenes.opera: t2va_opera_grand_stage -- a sung Italian aria with a lyrics pair: the singing one

rungs.dense: stock attention, no sage, no Sol, no LoRA (h3_text_to_video_dense_stamped_api)
rungs.solfp16: the sol rung with the sage node in its fp16 (most accurate) mode: sage runs the outer steps, so this is the cheap-insurance arm
rungs.pdd8: shipped PDD8 with sage auto + Sol (h3_text_to_video_pdd_api); its own ladder

prompts: named by bank id through the runner's @bank: value; the text lives only in prompt_bank/
run: bench/run_graph_arms.py --manifest bench/ladder_arms.json --runs 1 --seed 730451892 --hold-seed --no-alternate --out bench/results/<date>_ladder_arms.jsonl; then bench/blind_batch.py on the jsonl, score, bench/score_session.py
how_to_read: Compare rungs within a scene, never scenes against each other. The dense rung shows what the model itself does with a distant face or a small figure (blur and drift there are the model's own limit, per the owner); the question each higher rung answers is whether the speedup made THAT worse, and where.
